title: Snowy Wildlife ABC
hook: Different bodies meet the cold differently.
roundStructure: Round 1 lexical-semantic A-Z; Round 2 retrieval-action A-Z; 4+4+4+4+4+4+2 chunks
visualStyle: cute 3D snowy-wildlife storybook, soft snow fields and icy sky, recognizable animals, rounded clean forms

creativeFingerprint.pointOfView: a child comparing visible body features that help different animals live in cold places
creativeFingerprint.chorusFunction: group body strategies while preserving differences between mammals, birds, fish and context objects
creativeFingerprint.grooveMeter: gentle 3/4 feature-study sway with crisp target space
creativeFingerprint.round1Grammar: hand-written body-feature comparisons; nonliving and off-habitat mapping helpers are explicitly framed as context
creativeFingerprint.round2Grammar: feature cue -> recall beat -> target -> body-shape or safe pointing gesture
creativeFingerprint.sectionContrast: Verses stay sparse; chorus widens; retrieval strips back. soft bell sparkle after targets over a warm acoustic pulse
creativeFingerprint.signatureColor: soft bell sparkle after targets over a warm acoustic pulse
creativeFingerprint.authorialIntent: Compare cold-climate body solutions—fur, feather, flipper, broad paw, shaggy coat, tusk, diving body—while treating ice, tundra, boats and Xylophone as context rather than pretending every target has a biological adaptation.
creativeFingerprint.lyricIdentity: A child notices body covering and shape; recurring language uses fur, feather, flipper, layer, broad, compact, shaggy, surface and warm-body tool.
semanticArc: fur and feathers begin the comparison
sea mammals add flippers and body mass
context objects close the lesson without false biology
forbiddenGenericLanguage: cold-climate friends come sing with me
